newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola denies it sent troops into Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Angola denies it sent troops into Zaire.

text.p: Angola denied on Saturday charges by the Kinshasa government that Angolan troops had crossed into Zaire from the northern Cabinda enclave.
"These reports are false. There are no Angolan troops in Zaire. We deny this categorically," Angolan presidential spokesman Aldemiro Vaz de Conceicao told reporters.
Zaire's radio on Friday quoted a presidential statement accusing Angolan troops of crossing the border to back rebel troops advancing on Kinshasa to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko.
The radio said thousands of people had fled the Zairean village of Yema, close to the coastal city of Muanda, about 400 km (240 mile) west of Kinshasa.
Expatriate mining officials in Angola's northeastern Lunda Norte province said on Friday the Angolan army and Zaire rebels were performing joint military exercises on the Angolan side of the border.
The sources said the exercises were taking place near the border town of Dundo, where Rwandan refugees have been crossing into Angola's diamond-rich area from Zaire.

But Western diplomats in Luanda said the Angolan military activity in Zaire was part of the Angolan government's plans to clean out FLEC guerrilla separatists who have been fighting for oil-rich Cabinda's independence for years.
The diplomats said the guerrillas have bases in Zaire to the south and southeast of Cabinda.
Cabinda is separated from the rest of Angola by a strip of Zairean territory and bordered to the north by Congo.
FLEC, which is divided into more than 13 factions, was not party to a ceasefire agreement between the Angolan government and UNITA rebels in 1994 to end two decades of civil war.

UNITA, which is a strong ally of President Mobutu, held supply bases in Zaire during the Angolan war, but these have since been closed as the forces of Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila have slowly taken control of more than half of the country since he launched his military campaign against Mobutu in October last year.
